html:
The State of the Teutonic Order was a country ruled by a German order of crusading monks, the Teutonic Knights, along the south-east Baltic from the 1230s to 1525. On the map for 1279 to 1500 it covers Prussia and Livonia, roughly today's north-east Poland, Latvia and Estonia.

The order was founded at Acre in the Holy Land in the 1190s. In 1226 a Polish duke invited it to fight the pagan Prussians. In the Northern Crusades the knights conquered Prussia over fifty years and took over Livonia. German settlers and merchants followed; towns such as Danzig and Königsberg joined the Hanseatic League. From 1309 the grand master ruled from the vast brick castle of Marienburg.

Its long war was with pagan Lithuania, which turned into war with Poland as well. Poland and Lithuania crushed the order at the Battle of Grunwald in 1410, and in 1466 it lost western Prussia to Poland. In 1525 the grand master, Albert, turned Lutheran and made the rest a secular duchy, Prussia.
